assessment.nobel_worthiness: The observation of a scalar boson at 125 GeV completed the Standard Model and is arguably the most important discovery in particle physics of the century. The experimental half has never been recognised; the 2013 prize went to the theoretical prediction. This is the clearest case of a discovery that nature itself delivered.
assessment.attribution: ATLAS and CMS are collaborations of thousands. Della Negra, Jenni and Virdee were founding proposers and long-term leaders of the detector programmes, but the decisive contributions were distributed (spokespersons during 2012, trigger/analysis leaders, detector builders). A person-based configuration is imperfect and the committee would have to decide whether the three founders fairly represent the experiments or whether an organisation-oriented citation is needed.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature: two independent experiments, a decade of coupling and spin-parity measurements consistent with the Standard Model. Recognition is, if anything, overdue.
uncertainties: Whether founder-level credit to three individuals is considered fair given the collaboration structure.
Whether the committee wants to credit instrument leadership rather than the analysis teams that made the 2012 announcement.
I have not independently verified the exact role histories of the three credited individuals.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: IceCube opened neutrino astronomy by detecting a diffuse flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos, then associating neutrinos with the blazar TXS 0506+056 and later with the Galactic plane and NGC 1068. It is a new window on the universe built on a vision of instrumenting a cubic kilometre of Antarctic ice, and its results come directly from nature.
assessment.attribution: Halzen is the intellectual and scientific driver of IceCube; Spiering was a founding figure in neutrino telescopes (AMANDA, Baikal, IceCube) and the broader field. Credit is cleaner than for most large collaborations, though other pioneers (for example Baikal and DUMAND/AMANDA contributors) could be argued for. Two proposed names is workable.
assessment.maturity: Diffuse flux established around 2013 and confirmed in several independent channels; point-source evidence (2017-2023) is solid but still few sources. Timely, with room for further maturing.
uncertainties: Whether the source-identification results are robust enough versus the detector-and-diffuse-flux discovery alone.
Whether earlier pioneers' contributions (DUMAND, Baikal, AMANDA) are adequately reflected by two names.
Pioneer credit details are from my own background knowledge and unverified here.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Direct imaging of the shadow of M87* and Sgr A* gave horizon-scale images of black holes and showed strong-gravity consistency with general relativity. It sits near my own research interests and the existential appeal of seeing a black hole is real.
assessment.attribution: Doeleman led the EHT project and the VLBI technique at mm wavelengths; Falcke proposed the shadow imaging concept and the Sgr A* case; Zensus built the European VLBI infrastructure and leads the MPIfR effort. The large collaboration (over 300 people) means any trio is a simplification, and imaging algorithm and data-calibration contributors are not credited.
assessment.maturity: Results from 2019 and 2022 are recent; independent re-analyses and polarisation follow-ups support them, but only one array exists and the tests of GR are still modest in precision. The 2020 prize already honoured black-hole physics, which slightly lowers urgency.
uncertainties: Limited precision of the strong-field tests; the images do not yet discriminate against horizonless alternatives strongly.
Recognition may be premature compared with candidates whose confirmation has taken longer.
Attribution among Falcke, Zensus and Doeleman versus the algorithm and calibration leaders.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, born from Katori's magic-wavelength proposal, achieve fractional uncertainties near 1e-18 and have transformed timekeeping, tests of relativity through gravitational redshift across millimetres, and searches for dark-matter and variation of constants. The 2005 prize honoured the frequency comb; this is the successor discovery of clear importance.
assessment.attribution: Katori conceived the magic-wavelength lattice approach and first demonstrated it with Sr; Ye brought the clock to record accuracy and many-body engineering. Two laureates is a clean configuration, though the ion-clock community (Wineland-type approaches) and other lattice groups also contributed.
assessment.maturity: Over two decades of independent confirmation worldwide; performance is metrologically verified and still improving. Timing is good.
uncertainties: Overlap with ion clock and frequency-comb contributions already prized.
Whether the committee views metrology as a discovery or an advance in instrumentation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The theoretical prediction of flat bands at the magic angle and the experimental discovery of correlated insulators and superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene opened moire quantum materials, a large and productive field. The connection between prediction and observation is unusually direct.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the 2011 flat-band prediction; Jarillo-Herrero led the 2018 experiments (with Cao and others, who are not in the credited set). A theory-plus-experiment trio is natural, but the first-author experimentalist and the role of Pablo's group members are potential complications.
assessment.maturity: Observed since 2018 and reproduced by many groups. The nature of the superconducting pairing remains open. Eight years is short but not unusual for this physics.
uncertainties: The pairing mechanism of the superconductivity is still debated.
Recognition might be premature, and a decade of maturation could change the picture.
Whether Bistritzer, MacDonald and Jarillo-Herrero capture the decisive credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Spectroscopic detection of exoplanet atmospheres, beginning with sodium in HD 209458b, now extended by JWST to molecules and clouds, moves exoplanets from census to characterisation and bears directly on the question of life elsewhere, which I find to have real existential weight. The 2019 prize honoured the discovery of exoplanets, so this is a natural continuation.
assessment.attribution: Seager supplied early theory of transmission and atmospheric structure; Charbonneau made the first detection; Tinetti led later spectroscopic programmes and the Ariel mission. The field is crowded (Brown, Deming, Knutson, Swain and others) and the credited trio is not obviously decisive.
assessment.maturity: Basic detections are well confirmed; detailed interpretation (abundances, biosignatures) is evolving. JWST results are strengthening but still young.
uncertainties: Crowded credit with several comparable contributors excluded.
Atmospheric retrievals are model dependent.
Continuity with the 2019 prize may reduce appetite.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The 2005 numerical-relativity breakthroughs made stable binary black hole evolutions possible, producing the waveform templates that underpin gravitational-wave data analysis. It turned a long-standing theoretical problem into a precision tool, and has been validated by hundreds of detections.
assessment.attribution: Pretorius did the generalised-harmonic breakthrough; Campanelli and Baker (with their groups) independently introduced moving-puncture methods. Credit among the moving-puncture group (Campanelli, Lousto, Zlochower, Baker, Centrella, Van Meter) is split, which makes a fair three-person configuration difficult.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed in practice by LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA signals matching numerical waveforms. Mature, but the 2017 prize already centred on the detection.
uncertainties: Credit split between generalised harmonic and moving puncture approaches.
Whether a computational method counts as a discovery in the Nobel sense, since the committee seeks discoveries rather than techniques.
Details of who first published remain from my memory rather than verified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Inflation explains flatness, homogeneity and the origin of structure, and its prediction of a nearly scale-invariant spectrum of adiabatic perturbations has been confirmed by COBE, WMAP and Planck. It is one of the most consequential ideas in cosmology, with an existential dimension about the origin of everything.
assessment.attribution: Starobinsky, Guth and Linde proposed the models; Mukhanov (with Chibisov) computed the quantum origin of perturbations, which is the testable heart of the idea. Leaving Mukhanov out of a three-person set would be hard to defend, and the committee is limited to three; choosing between these four is a real allocation problem.
assessment.maturity: The spectral tilt is confirmed, but inflation itself is not: primordial gravitational waves have not been seen, and the alternatives and the measure problem persist. My own work on trans-Planckian effects shows how sensitive the conclusions can be to unconfirmed assumptions. I am wary of rewarding an elegant idea before a decisive clue from nature, though big ideas can take long to prove.
uncertainties: No detection of primordial B-modes; the tensor-to-scalar ratio is only bounded.
Four-way credit problem with at most three laureates.
Trans-Planckian and measure-problem concerns about the theoretical framework.
Premature unless a decisive observation arrives.
